reasoning_quality_informational.v1_root_problem: Billing dispute tickets have roughly doubled since August 2026 (F-04: ~600/month Jun-Jul to ~1180-1260/month Aug-Sep), and the best-supported mechanism in current evidence is that field manual-meter-read route completion for ~9200 accounts fell below target (0.88 vs 0.95, F-01) during the same period, driving estimate substitution that accounts for the 41% of disputed bills built on ESTIMATED reads (F-02). This mechanism does not explain the majority (59%) of disputed bills, which are on ACTUAL reads, leaving that larger segment's cause open pending further investigation (billing rule changes, AMI data quality, or genuine usage increase).
reasoning_quality_informational.v2_root_problem: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled since August 2026 (F-04). For the 41% of disputed bills on ESTIMATED reads (1240/3025, F-02), the best-supported mechanism is that billing-import rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 with no unit scaling (F-10), compares raw AMI register values against 12-month m3 history; v4.2-firmware meters (rollout June 2026) report values in 0.1 m3 units versus v3.x's m3 units (F-11), so BV-17 misclassifies valid, on-time v4.2 reads as high-consumption and rejects them (1184/1240 = 95.5%, F-09), forcing estimate substitution. This mechanism does not explain the remaining 59% of disputed bills (1785/3025) on ACTUAL reads, whose cause is still open.
reasoning_quality_informational.ideal_final_problem: BV-17 validation rejects valid firmware-v4.2 AMI reads (unit-scale mismatch on H-MDMS-BILL) and substitutes estimates.
